 Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Barnes, who was limited during Sunday’s practice, will miss a second straight game with an adductor injury. With Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) also out, Allen Graves could potentially make his first NBA start. Even if he doesn’t, the rookie’s playing time should increase.

 Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Barnes will miss his third consecutive game with an adductor injury. Collin Murray-Boyles could move into the starting lineup in Barnes’ absence.

 Scottie Barnes (adductor) and Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) were limited at Sunday’s practice and will be questionable for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Barnes and Quickley sat out Friday’s win over the Bucks, which led to Jakob Poeltl returning to the starting lineup and Jamal Shead filling in for Quickley. That’s likely to remain the case on Monday if Barnes and Quickley can’t play. The absences would also raise the fantasy ceilings of RJ Barrett, Ja’Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles.

 Scottie Barnes (left adductor, groin) will not play against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Scottie Barnes will miss his first game of the season with an injury. Look for Collin Murray-Boyles take on more usage in this game. We could also see a bump from Jakob Poeltl, Jamison Battle or Allen Graves with this injury. If there’s an add in redraft leagues, Poeltl is the most sensible one.

 Scottie Barnes (groin) is questionable to play against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Barnes wasn’t initially on the injury report, but he now may miss a game for the first time this season. With Collin Murray-Boyles already in the starting lineup, Jakob Poeltl would likely return to the opening unit if Barnes is out.

 Scottie Barnes got himself 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, six assists, three steals, a three, and five turnovers in loss to Nuggets. 
 Scottie filled up the box score despite not having the greatest night scoring the ball. The Raptors as a whole didn’t do a great job defensively in this game which resulted in their blowout. Scottie has had so many good performances recently that there’s no need to panic. The next opportunity to bounce back will be against the Bucks on Friday.

 Scottie Barnes accumulated 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 8-of-15 FTs), 15 rebounds, eight assists and two steals in Monday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Barnes appeared to aggravate his sore left hip during the third quarter, but he returned to the game after some time on the bench. And it’s a good thing he did, as the Raptors forward was outstanding in the fourth quarter. Barnes recorded 15 points, eight rebounds, one assist and two steals in the quarter, helping the Raptors erase a 13-point deficit to win by seven. Barnes struggled at the foul line, but that was his only negative on his final stat line.

 Scottie Barnes (hip) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Barnes popped up on the injury report Monday afternoon as questionable with left hip tightness. While the injury doesn’t sound overly serious, Barnes could be on the wrong side of questionable here. If he’s ruled out, Collin Murray-Boyles could move into the starting lineup. 
 Scottie Barnes

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals. 
 Barnes’ mid-range mastery helped him score 29 points, and he’s scored at least 28 in three straight and four of his last five games. The exception was the October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, in which the Raptors’ star went scoreless. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) out for a few weeks, Barnes will need to shoulder more responsibility on both ends of the floor. And he’s shown the ability to do that in the past.

 Isaiah Collier produced 17 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 While Keyonte George’s ankle injury did not result in a start for Collier, his role did take on added importance. The Jazz guard had an efficient night, shooting 4-of-4 from three and committing two turnovers before fouling out. If George misses more time, Collier will be worth a look in deep leagues, even if his shooting against the Heat wasn’t his norm. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ace Bailey accounted for 23 points (10-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 Bailey enjoyed one of the best offensive performances of his young NBA career on Tuesday. Shooting 66.7 percent from the field, the second-year forward finished with a season-high 23 points. After scoring at least 20 points in 16 games as a rookie, this was his first 20-point game of the 2026-27 campaign. Already without Jaren Jackson Jr., the Jazz didn’t have Lauri Markkanen on Tuesday, and those absences have raised Bailey’s short-term ceiling. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darryn Peterson finished Tuesday’s loss to the Heat with 25 points (10-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
 With no Keyonte George, Peterson made his first start at point guard for the Jazz on Tuesday. While he committed five turnovers and ultimately fouled out, this was a good night overall for the rookie. Peterson scored efficiently and dished out a few assists in his 31 minutes. His fantasy ceiling should be raised slightly for as long as George remains sidelined.

 Pelle Larsson accounted for 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 Larsson has started Miami’s last two games, recording solid stat lines in each. The question worth considering is whether this move will stick for the long haul, or only as long as it takes Andrew Wiggins to find his offensive form. Against the Jazz, Wiggins scored 13 points on 5-of-8 shooting but did not record any other stats. Even with his reserve role at the start of the season, Larsson has been the superior fantasy option.

 Davion Mitchell recorded 19 points (5-of-13 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 The dilemma for fantasy managers rostering Mitchell: sell high or hold? “Off Night” has been highly productive for the Heat this season, and Miami’s lack of depth at point guard means he’ll play heavy minutes. However, those who aren’t convinced Mitchell can play at this level for a full season should strongly consider looking into what he could fetch in a trade. Mitchell finished Tuesday’s victory two assists shy of a double-double, making up for the low field-goal percentage.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 30 points (12-of-21 FGs, 5-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz.
 Initially questionable for Tuesday’s game with a sprained right wrist, Antetokounmpo got up 21 shots against the Jazz. He scored 15 points in each half, shooting 7-of-14 from the field in the second half. Giannis’ dominant performance helped offset Bam Adebayo’s (11/8/4/4/2) 1-of-8 shooting from the field. The Heat head home, with a Friday/Saturday back-to-back against the Cavaliers and Pistons up next.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Suns.
 While not a player who absolutely has to be rostered in 12-team leagues, Jones has been productive enough to provide reliable deep-league value. Against the Suns, his final stat line lacked only an assist, and he’s now shooting 17-of-36 from beyond the arc. Jones would help his fantasy value if he could consistently provide steals; six of his 10 steals this season have been recorded in two games.

 Rui Hachimura tallied 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Suns.
 Hachimura shot 3-of-5 from beyond the arc on Tuesday, and the two steals matched his season high. Unfortunately, his production outside of points and rebounds remains limited, and the Clippers forward is shooting below 40 percent from the field. Hachimura’s status as a starter is why he’s rostered in 62 percent of Yahoo leagues, but that number may decrease once Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is cleared to play.

 Garland and the Clippers had a tough night in Phoenix, so much so that none of the starters played in the fourth quarter. For those willing to punt turnovers, Garland has provided good fantasy value this season. He and the Clippers will look to bounce back on Friday when they host the Thunder.

 Gillespie was one of five Suns reserves to finish Tuesday’s 133-110 victory in double figures. In addition to shooting 4-of-9 from three, he recorded a team-high eight assists.
